correctness.rationale: The claim is finite and fully quantified over the 2048 rotation classes of binary order-five de Bruijn cycles. Every such class is a unique Euler tour anchored at the sole 00000 edge of the 16-vertex/32-edge de Bruijn digraph. An independent complete enumeration of all 65536 local pairings gives exactly the same 2048 circuits. Signed autocorrelation and mismatching-bit arithmetic produce identical best-over-32-cuts/max-over-31-lags distributions. Exhaustive exact-integer tests verify all 11 bins, extrema, moments, symmetry orbits, minimizing-cut multiplicities, and the periodic/aperiodic splitting identity. Both methods and all expected values are in the standalone included VERIFY.py. No infinite-order claims are drawn from the finite census.

originality.rationale: The inspected closest primary study of all 2048 de Bruijn cycles (Spinsante–Andrenacci–Gambi 2011) tabulates periodic correlation sidelobe statistics, not a minimum over cuts of aperiodic correlation peaks. Its periodic level-4 class contains 12 cycles, while the new aperiodic optimally cut level-4 class contains 32, and no implication from the former statement yields the new histogram. Katz–van der Linden (2021) proves aperiodic PSL bounds for the distinct Golay–Rudin–Shapiro recursion and does not enumerate de Bruijn cycles. Related recorded research on periodic autocorrelation energy, plus published general phase-code literature, addresses different statistics. Multiple actual research-index and primary-source searches found no equivalent or dominating statement, though unknown literature remains possible.
residual_risks: An equivalent exact table could exist in non-indexed communications/cyclic-code literature, including alternate names such as phase cut, circular shift, or truncated sidelobe.

value.rationale: In a cyclic spreading sequence the cut is physically meaningful when a finite nonperiodic block is transmitted, because aperiodic autocorrelation sidelobes change with the cut even though periodic sidelobes do not. The complete exact spectrum of optimal phase choices for the classical full 2048-cycle de Bruijn order-five family supplies a motivated natural design invariant, sharp extrema and all attainability gaps/multiplicities, and exact symmetry classification. It is not a known-table recomputation: the older 2011 table concerns periodic sidelobes and a prior energy spectrum concerns periodic squared sums, neither the new minimax operation. Finite scope does not preclude mathematical value; the statement makes no unproved future or physical deployment claims.
